verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Encoding only. The Lean takes K : Set (ℝ × ℝ × ℝ) and writes the containment pointwise as the hypothesis `∀ z ∈ K, 0 < z.1` rather than as a set inclusion; the rewriting is `Set.subset_def`, i.e. K ⊆ {z | 0 < z.1} ↔ ∀ z ∈ K, 0 < z.1. The paper's ℝ³ with coordinates (a, b_s, w) is the nested product with (z.1, z.2.1, z.2.2), the convention used throughout `compact_large_lag`. One direction of generality: the paper says 'For every nonempty compact set K', while the Lean assumes only `IsCompact K` (its docstring says 'The theorem also covers an empty set'), so the Lean hypothesis is the weaker one and the surrounding theorem is correspondingly more general; nothing in the paper's claim is lost.
